criteria.text: Is the agent's stated reasoning consistent with the edits it actually made and the feedback it received (no post-hoc rationalization, no lucky guess)?
Did each refinement stage (lint, test) do real, feedback-responsive work toward the solution rather than cosmetic or no-op changes?

The u8→Inst conversion maps exactly 0x01→Print, 0x02→Load, 0x03→Exception, 0x04→Initialize, 0x05→Exit, 0x06→Execute, and every other value→Unknown, implemented as a general table/match (not special-cased), and is the inverse of casting an Inst to its u8 discriminant.

Message construction records payload byte length in a 16-bit size field: 0 when data is absent, and a payload longer than 65535 is explicitly clamped to 65535 (warning to stderr) rather than truncated by a direct usize→u16 cast or a panic; len() returns size as usize.

send_msg writes, in order and big-endian: 1 instruction byte, then a 2-byte size, then the raw data bytes (nothing when data is absent); e.g. a Print message carrying "hello" emits exactly [1,0,5,104,101,108,108,111]. Size must be 2 bytes, not 1 or 4/usize, and field order must not be reversed.

recv_msg reads exactly 1 instruction byte, exactly 2 big-endian size bytes, then exactly `size` data bytes using read-exactly semantics (not read/read_to_end), short-circuits to a data-less message when size is 0, decodes the instruction via the Inst mapping, and propagates I/O errors.
A helper obtains a free local TCP port by binding to 127.0.0.1:0 and reading the assigned port from the socket's local address.

In REPL mode the VM constructor picks a free port, loads the embedded REPL server script, substitutes both the chosen port and the dump module name (path separators converted to dots) into it, spawns the Python interpreter on it, retries the TCP connection until it succeeds, sets a read timeout from config, and stores the connected stream; in non-REPL mode no stream is created and the compiler is always built from config.
cfg/cfg_mut expose the compiler's config and initialize/clear delegate to the compiler.

Batch exec reads input, compiles in exec mode, writes warnings to config output, and returns an ExitStatus carrying the executed child's exit code (defaulting to 0 when absent) plus the warning count — not a fixed/always-zero value.

eval compiles source in eval mode, sends an Execute message with the generated Python script bytes to the server, receives one response, and dispatches by instruction with distinct semantics: Exception→system-exit error, Initialize→re-init generator and take payload as text, Print→take payload as text, and Exit/Load/Execute/Unknown→clean termination as unexpected. Results are computed via the real server round-trip, not faked in Rust per test string.

eval appends the textual result to accumulated warnings, strips a trailing "None" so a unit/None result shows nothing, and when type display is enabled appends the last expression's type (and, for a definition, its identifier).

expect_block parses the source and classifies continuation: an ExpectNextLine error's sub-message maps to a BlockKind, an unterminated triple-quote error yields a multi-line-string block, other errors yield an error kind, and on successful parse source containing Class is a class definition otherwise no special block.

PackageManagerRunner::run verifies the external poise tool is available (emitting an error and non-zero status if missing), then invokes it with inherited stdio and the config's runtime args, returning its exit status.
